subject: sociology
title: Feminism Exam Stretch
welcome_lead: Time to evaluate. Is feminism finished, fragmented, or still vital? Build an essay-worthy judgement here.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology exam stretch evaluating feminism with postmodern and post-feminist critiques.
final_note: Strong evaluations name a current example: #MeToo, Black Lives Matter, board-room ratios.

concepts.def: Claim equality is achieved; feminism is obsolete.
Faludi: media pushback against feminist gains.
Women erased or trivialised by media.
Harmful norms also damaging men and boys.
Researcher reflecting on their own gender bias.

walkthroughs.body_html: Post-feminists argue equality has been won and feminism is outdated. Critics like Susan Faludi reply that there is a steady backlash in media and politics, and stats (pay gap, board seats) prove gaps remain.
Postmodern feminists argue 'woman' is not one fixed identity. Race, class, sexuality and disability all reshape experience. This links to intersectionality from Crenshaw.
Identify the strand (liberal/radical/Marxist/Black). Add a thinker. Give a current example (#MeToo, pay-gap data). Offer a counter (post-feminism, New Right). End with a clear judgement.

numericals.q: In which year did the #MeToo movement go viral globally?

free_texts.q: What single word names the claim that feminism's job is now done?
